I see programming as a creative art, like painting or sculpture, but with bytes instead of paint or clay. I've been doing it for about 40 years and still learning! Like any artist you can expect criticism and rejection of your early work. My advice, such as it is, would be to publish as soon as you have anything at all that vaguely "works" and be prepared with a thick skin. There's a lot of really crap software on the App Store! Don't hold back until you think something is "complete" otherwise you might never release it (nothing's perfect; can always be improved). Publishing an app is a never-ending journey, not a destination.

In this case, start with an app which just displays the front page of Voat (no login, no posting, no messaging etc) and publish it: version 1. It must be a free download, of course, and don't be tempted to include ads at this stage. Learn your way around the Apple app submission process. Post the App Store link on Voat and ask for feedback. Fix the bugs (there is always another bug) in version 1.1. Try to get this very simple functionality working as prefectly as possible. What happens if Voat goes down? What happens if the iPhone isn't connected to the network? Then start on version 2: lets you log in and see your own front page. Version 3: lets you post submissions. Version 4: edit user settings... etc.

Publish at every little step of the way. Understand "regression testing", i.e. checking that adding something new didn't break something that used to work. Gradually you will acquire users and their feedback can guide you.

This might sound discouraging, but I'd completely forget about making any income from the app until you're a long way down the line - i.e. keep it free for download and no advertising. Otherwise you will discourage your early users from trying it out.

Needless to say I wish you the best of luck. Do keep me posted, and keep hitting me up with questions if you have any. Looking forward to that first App Store link :)
